# The Twenty-First Chapter.
## Concerning the Third Day.

->1.<-

Although the *Spirit* in the writings of *Moses* has kept the deepest mysteries hidden and concealed within the literal text <note>original: "Letter"; Böhme often distinguishes between the "Letter" (literal meaning) and the "Spirit" (inner mystical meaning) of Scripture</note>, yet everything is described so very regularly that there is no defect at all in its order.

2. For when God, through the Word, had created Heaven and Earth, and had separated the Light from the Darkness and given a place to each of them, then each presently began its birth <note>original: "Geniture"; the process of generating or bringing forth life</note> and its operating or working.

3. On the **First Day**, God drove together [or compacted] the corrupt <term>Salitter</term> <note>Salitter: Böhme’s term for the fundamental divine substance or "salt-niter" of the universe, which can be either holy or "corrupted" by wrath</note> which became so through the kindling of His wrath. I say, God then drove it together or created it through the strong Spirit; for the word **Schuff** <note>original: "Schuff"; the German word *schuf* means "created," but Böhme interprets the sound of the word as a "shoving" or driving together of matter</note> signifies here a "driving together" or "compaction."

4. In this driving together or compaction of the corrupted wrath-Salitter, King *Lucifer* was also—as a powerless prince together with his angels—driven into the "hole" of the wrath-Salitter. He was driven into that place where the outward, half-dead tangibility <note>original: "comprehenſibility"; referring to the physical world that can be perceived and grasped by the senses</note> is generated, which is the place or space between the nature-goddess, the *Moon*, and the dead *Earth*.

5. Now when this was done, the Deep became clear,

Accordingly, there passed the time of *one revolution*, or of *one day*, which contains twenty-four hours.

6. During the *Second Day*, the sharp *separation* began; the *incomprehensible chasm* <note>original: "Cliffe"; here meaning a "cleft" or abyss (German: *Kluft*) that separates two distinct realms</note> between the *Wrath* and the *Love* of *Light* was made. Thus King *Lucifer* was firmly and strongly *bolted up* into the House of *Darkness* and was reserved for the final *Judgment*.

7. In this way, the water of *Life* was also separated from the water of *Death*. Yet, they are joined to one another in this temporal world like *Body* and *Soul*, and yet neither of them can fully grasp <note>original: "comprehend"; used here in the sense of one substance containing or penetrating another</note> the other. The *Heaven* which was made out of the midst or center of the *water* is the *divide* <note>original: "Cliffe"</note> between them, so that the tangible or physical water is a *Death*, and the intangible or spiritual water is the *Life*.

8. Thus, the incomprehensible *Spirit*, which *is God*, now rules everywhere in this world and *fills all things*. The tangible world depends upon Him and dwells in the *Darkness*; it can neither see, hear, smell, nor feel the incomprehensible Spirit, but it sees His works and is a *destroyer* of them.

9. And now, when God had bound up the *Devil* in the *Darkness* through the *sealing* of the *Heaven*—which *Heaven* is present everywhere in all places—He began again His wonderful *birth* or *generation* <note>original: "Geniture"; Böhme's term for the ongoing process of divine creation and manifestation</note> in the *seventh* nature-spirit, and everything was generated again just as *it had been from eternity*.

According to this Third Birth, the earth shall be purged and cleansed at the end of this time and shall be set or put again into its *original* place; but the wrath will remain in death.

For the *first* qualifying or fountain *spirit* is the astringent <term>original: "Astringent"; the contracting, cold, and binding force.</term>, cold, sharp, and hard birth or generation <term>original: "Geniture"; the internal process of birth or the natural constitution of a thing.</term>, and that belongs to the first day in the astral birth. The astrologers call it the *Saturnine* <note>Referring to the influence of the planet Saturn, traditionally associated with coldness, darkness, and restriction.</note>, which was performed on the first day. For in that day, the hard, dry, sharp earth and stones came to be and were incorporated or compacted together. Moreover, the strong firmament of heaven was also generated then; and the heart of the seven spirits of God stood hidden in that hard sharpness.

130. Astrologers attribute the *second* day to *Sol* <note>original: "Sol"; Latin for the Sun.</note> or the Sun, but it belongs to *Jupiter* to speak of it astrologically. For on the second day, the light broke forth out of the *heart* of the seven qualifying or fountain spirits through the hard quality of the heaven, and caused a mitigation or softening in the hard water of the heaven; and the light began shining in that meekness and softening.

131. And then the meekness and the hard water separated from each other, and the hardness remained in its hard place, like a hard death, and the meekness or softness penetrated through the hardness by the power of the light.

132. And this now is the *water of life*, which is generated in the light of God out of the hard death. And thus the light of God in the *sweet water*...

## Morning Redness in the Rising.
<note>original: "Morning-Rednesse"; this is the English translation of the book's original German title, *Morgenröte*, which refers to the light of God's grace rising in the soul.</note>

1. For here, even a very simple person will be able to see and comprehend or understand the Being of God.

2. The reader should not make himself blind through his *unbelief* and dull *understanding*; for here I bring in the whole of nature with all her children as a *witness* and *demonstration*. And if you are rational, then look all around you and examine yourself; also consider yourself rightly, and then you will soon find from what *spirit* I write.

3. For my part, I will obediently perform the command of the *spirit*; only you must take care, and do not allow yourself to be shut out by an open door: for here the gates of knowledge stand open to you.

4. And though the *spirit* will indeed go against the current of some *astrologers*, that is no great matter to me, for I am bound to obey *God* rather than *men*. They are blind concerning the *spirit*, and if they will not see, then they may remain blind still.

22. Behold! I tell you a mystery: as soon as the door is set *wide* open to its full angle, all useless, firmly-nailed, sticking bolts or bars will be cast away. 54. 55. But if someone who does *not* know the way *pushes* through the wrath into Love, then they are like the person who pushed through *by* their knowledge. But he who has *Love* in his heart, and leads a merciful, meek, and humble life, and *fights* against malice and hatred, and *pushes* through the wrath of God into the Light—he lives with God and is *one spirit* with God.

57. For God requires no other service but that His creature, who exists within *His Body* <note>Boehme often describes the universe as the "body" of God</note>, does not slide back away from *Him*, **but remains holy, just as He is.**

# The Twenty-Third Chapter.

## *Of the Deep above the Earth.*

->I.<-

When man beholds the <term>Deep</term> <note>original: "Deep"; referring to the vast expanse of the sky or the firmament above the Earth.</note> above the Earth, he sees nothing but *stars* and *clouds* of water. Then he thinks, "Surely there must be another place where the *Deity* presents or shows itself, together with the *heavenly* and *Angelical Governance*." He insists on having the Deep, along with its <term>rule</term> <note>original: "regiment"; referring to the systematic government or dominion of the natural world.</note> or dominion, separated from the *Deity*; for there he sees nothing but *stars*, and the rule or dominion in between is fire, air, and water.

2. Then he immediately thinks, "God has made this in this way out of or from his *predestined purpose*, *out of nothing*." How then *can* God be within this being? Or, *can* that be God Himself? He continually imagines that this is only a house where God rules and dwells by His *Spirit*. He thinks God cannot be such a God whose being consists in the power of *this* government or dominion.

3. Many will dare to say, "What *kind* of God would that be, whose body, being, and power or virtue stands or consists in fire, air, water, and earth?"

# The Gate of the Holy Trinity.

67. **The entire Birth or Generation** <note>original: "Geniture"; the eternal process of divine creation and becoming.</note> which is the Heaven of all Heavens, as well as this world—which is *within* the Body of the whole—as well as the place of the Earth and of all creatures, and whatever you can think of: **all of that together is God the Father.** He has neither beginning nor end; and wherever and whatever you think upon, even in the smallest circle that can be imagined, there is the *entire* Birth or Generation of God, perfectly, incessantly, and irresistibly.

68. But if the light is extinguished in any creature or in any place, then the austere Birth or Generation <note>original: "austere Geniture"; in Böhme’s theology, this refers to the harsh, rigorous, or wrathful quality of nature that exists when the light is withdrawn.</note> is *there*, which lies hidden within the Light in the innermost kernel. **And this is now the First Part.**

69. **The second part or the second Person is the Light,** which is continually generated from or out of all powers, and enlightens all the powers of the *Father* once again, and has the fountain of all powers. But it is distinguished from the Father as a *distinct Person*, in that it cannot encompass the Birth or Generation of the Father, and yet is the Father’s *Son*, who is always generated from or out of the Father. You have an example of this in all the kindled *fires* in this world; just consider them.

6. I cannot write this into your heart at all, for it is not within every man’s capacity, understanding, or grasp <note>original: "apprehension"</note>—especially where the spirit stands in the "house of wrath" and does not harmonize <note>original: "qualifie"; Boehme’s term for things sharing the same quality or operating in the same spiritual state</note>, operate, or unite with the Light of God. 7. Behold and consider a *tree*: on the outside, it has a hard, coarse *rind* or *bark* which is dead, numb, and without growth <note>original: "Vegetation"</note>. Yet it is not *completely* dead, but is in a state of frailty or weakness <note>original: "imbecillity"</note>. There is a great difference between it and the body of the tree, which grows just beneath the rind or bark. *But the body has its living power; it breaks forth through the withered rind and generates many beautiful young bodies or twigs, all of which remain within the old body.*

8. But the *rind* is as if it were dead and cannot understand <note>original: "comprehend"</note> the *life* of the tree. It only hangs upon it and serves as a *cover* for the tree, in which worms harbor and eventually destroy the tree.

9. And the whole house of this world is just like this: the outward darkness is the house of God’s wrath, where the devils dwell. It is rightly called the house of death, for the holy Light of God has died within it.

### Chapter XXIV. Of the Incorporating of the Stars.

You cannot see Heaven with your physical eyes; for the blue or azure sphere which you see above *is not Heaven*, but is only the old body, which may justly be called ***corrupted Nature.***

20. Though it seems there is a blue or azure sphere *above* the stars, by which the location of this world is closed off and shut out from the *holy Heaven*—as people have thought *until now*—it is *not so*. Instead, it is ***the superior water of Nature*** <note>original: "superiour water of Nature"; a reference to the "waters above the firmament" mentioned in Genesis, which Boehme interprets as a refined, spiritualized element</note>, which is much brighter than the water below the Moon. When the Sun shines through the deep space, it appears as a light-blue or azure color.

21. But how deep or how large the extent of this world is, *no one* knows, even though some *natural philosophers*, mathematicians, astronomers, or astrologers have attempted to measure the Deep with *their* measurements of circles. Their measuring is only guesswork, or an attempt to measure something that is tangible or palpable—it is as if someone tried to grasp the wind in their fist.

22. But the true Heaven is everywhere, all around us, *up to this very time* and until the Last Judgment Day. Likewise, the wrath-house of Hell and of Death is also in this world *everywhere*, even to the Last Judgment Day.

# **Of the Whole Body of this Astral World.** Chapter 25.

46. Dear Reader, I understand the *astrologers’* meanings and sayings full well, and I have perused their writings also, and taken notice of how they describe the course of the *Sun* and *stars*. I do not despise this, but hold it to be for the most part good and right.

47. But that I write differently than they do in some things, I do not do out of self-will, conceit, or mere supposition—doubting whether it be so or not. I dare not have any doubt here, nor can any man instruct me in this matter.

48. I have not gained my knowledge through study. Indeed, I have read of the order and *position* of the *seven planets* in the books of astrologers and find them to be very correct; but the Root—how they came to be and from what they proceeded—I cannot learn from any man. For they do not know it, nor was I present when God created them.

49. But because the Doors of the Deep, the Gates of Wrath, and the Chambers of Death are set open in my spirit through the Love of God, the spirit, *therefore*, must necessarily look through them.

50. And accordingly, I find that the Birth or Geniture of Nature <term>geniture</term> <note>original: "Geniture of Nature"; Böhme uses this term to describe the ongoing process of birth and "becoming" within the natural world</note> remains to this day and generates itself just as it first began. Whatever rises up in this world—whether humans, beasts, trees, herbs, grass, mineral ores, or whatever it may be—all rise up in such a quality, manner, and form. Also, every life, be it good or bad, takes its origin in this way.

51. For this is the *Right* or *Law* of the Deity: that every life in the body of God should generate itself in one manner or uniform way. Though it is done through many various *imaginings* <note>original: "Imagings"; in this context, the specific forms or internal "images" that the divine spirit projects into physical reality</note>, yet the *life*

# The Twenty-Sixth Chapter

## *Of the Planet Saturn*

-> 1. <-

Saturn—that cold, sharp, austere, and astringent ruler—does not take its beginning or origin from the *Sun*. For it has the chamber of death within its power and is a dryer-up of all powers, from which physicality <note>original: "Corporeity"</note> originates.

2. For just as the *Sun* is the heart of life and the origin of all spirits in the body of this world, so Saturn is the source of all physicality <note>original: "corporeity"</note> and comprehensibility or tangibility. The whole body of this world exists within the power of these two planets. There cannot be *any* creature, any formation <note>original: "imaging"</note>, or any movement <note>original: "mobilitie"</note> without the power of these two in the natural body of this world.

57. And this is the Body of the Deep, or the very real Chamber of Death.

58. But now, in this dark valley, there are the seven spirits of God, which have neither beginning nor end; and no one of them is the first, second, third, or last.

Instead, those seven spirits each generate one another, from eternity to eternity.

60. The *first* dominion or government exists or consists in the Body of all things—that is, in the whole Deep, or Being of all beings. It possesses the seven spirits within itself in every corner and place, holding them as its own property, indivisibly and irresistibly.

# Of Man and the Stars.

74. Just as the Deep <note>original: "Deepe"; the vast, hidden spiritual foundation of the universe</note>—or the house of this world—is a dark house where the whole of materiality <note>original: "Corporeity"</note> generates itself, and is therefore very thick, dark, anxious, and half-dead, taking its movement from the planets and stars which ignite the body in the outermost birth-process <note>original: "Geniture"; the ongoing process of creation and manifestation in nature</note>—from which arises the mobility of the elements, as well as the shape and being of every creature—so too the human house of flesh is a *dark valley*. Within it, there is indeed the anguish of the birth of life; it always strives upward, intending to elevate itself into the *Light*, from which *Life* might ignite itself.

### Note

> I inform the reader who loves God that this
> book, the **Aurora, or Morning Redness** <note>Böhme’s first book, written in 1612, which circulated in manuscript before he was silenced by local authorities</note>, was not finished;
> for the Devil intended to stop
> and suppress it when he perceived that the
> Day would break forth within it. And
> the **Day** has clearly hurried after the
> Morning Redness, so that it has become very
> bright. There are still about thirty
> sheets missing from the end of it. But because the storm <note>Refers to the intense persecution Böhme faced from Gregorius Richter, the pastor of Görlitz, which led to a years-long ban on his writing</note> has
> broken them off, it was not finished;
> and in the meantime, Day has arrived,
> so that the **Morning Redness** has passed
> away, and since that time, the work has
> continued in the light of Day. And it shall remain so, as
> **an eternal remembrance**,
> since the deficiency here is supplied in the
> * other books <note>Referring to the titles listed in the marginal note</note>.

->Jacob Böhme<-
->1620<-

->Note.<-

The *Dawning* or *Morning Redness* <note>original: "Morning-Rednesse"; the title of Böhme's first book, *Aurora*</note> rises up from *Infancy* and *Childhood*, and shows or demonstrates the *Creation* of all *Beings*, but *very mystically* and *not sufficiently clear*, but full of *Magical Understanding*; for there are some *Mysteries* within it which are yet to come to pass.

->Note.<-

This is the deep, hidden *Magical Book* which the *Author* at that time could not make clearer, but may now do so through the *Grace of God*, 1621.

->Note.<-

This book is written in a *Magical sense* or *understanding* for the *Author himself* only, who knew of no other *Readers*. He supposed he made this work *only for himself*, but *God* has disposed it otherwise.

->Note.<-

The *Author* expressed the first syllable *MER* in the word *MERCURIUS* <note>Latin for Mercury; in Böhme’s alchemy, it represents the active, transformative spirit</note> with an *A*, as *MAR*, *MARCURIUS*—not without a special *Mystical* cause involving the first *Vowel A*. But because the *self-conceited*, who consider themselves *wise in their own Reason*, dislike it—accounting it as nothing more than a *common country expression*—the transcriber of the *German copy* <note>original: "High Dutch Copie"</note> from which this was translated wrote it according to the commonly accepted word, *MERCURIUS*.

### Note.

The Author expressed the first syllable MER, in the word MERCURIUS <note>Mercury, a key term in Böhme's alchemy representing the "working power" of nature</note>, with an A, as MAR, MARCURIUS. He did this for a special mystical reason, using the first vowel A.
